summary: A small, fast systems language written to build Unix. Nearly every operating system, database and language runtime still rests on C, and most later languages borrowed its syntax.

icon.licence: CC0 1.0 (the mark itself belongs to its owner)

image.alt: Brian Kernighan’s handwritten “hello, world” in C

events.note: Dennis Ritchie creates C at Bell Labs as a successor to the B language.

events.label: Unix in C
events.note: Version 4 Unix ships with its kernel largely rewritten in C.

events.label: K&R book
events.note: Kernighan and Ritchie publish "The C Programming Language", the informal standard for a decade.

events.label: ANSI C
events.note: ANSI ratifies the first standard, X3.159-1989, known as C89.

events.label: C99
events.note: C99 adds inline functions and variable-length arrays.

events.label: C11
events.note: C11 adds threads and atomic operations.

events.label: C23
events.note: C23 adds new keywords and type inference with auto.
